Predictions

Two predictive models trained on the full catalog. These do not change with the filters above.

Forecast: monthly titles added

Model: average of the last 12 months, chosen because it beat ARIMA, exponential smoothing and trend models in a rolling backtest. The band is an 80% interval built from the model's real backtest errors.

Audience classifier

Gradient boosting model predicting Kids (G, PG, TV-Y, TV-Y7, TV-G, TV-PG), Teens (PG-13, TV-14) or Adults (R, NC-17, TV-MA) from genres, country, format and dates. Scores are out-of-fold: each title was scored by a model that never saw it.

What the classifier shows

How to read the model results.

    Find similar titles

    Content-based recommender: titles are compared on genres, director, country, type, audience and decade (TF-IDF with weighted cosine similarity). Type a title to see its six closest matches.

      Rating review list

      Titles where the classifier is at least 70% confident that the title belongs to a very different audience than its rating says. These are not errors; they are candidates for a quick human check. Many turn out to be correct (for example, family-friendly stand-up comedians), and many reveal weak metadata (titles tagged only with the generic genre "Movies").

      Business recommendations

      Based on catalog data only (what Netflix offers, not what people watch), so each recommendation should be validated with viewing data before acting on it.

      About this dashboard. Data: Netflix titles dataset, cleaned in Task 1 (8,786 titles after removing duplicates). Built with Python (pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels) and Plotly.js.
      • 2021 is a partial year. Year comparisons use full years where possible.
      • Each title lists one production country, so co-productions count only for the listed country.
      • About 29% of titles have no director listed, mostly TV shows.
      • The dataset has no plot descriptions or viewing data, which limits the recommender and the classifier.
